Who is Jeff?: Jeff is a Domestic Shorthair cat who lives in southern New Hampshire.
Can I meet Jeff?: If you're reading this, that means that you've already met Jeff. I'm sure he's happy that you're here!
Okay, but can I actually meet Jeff?: No, sorry. Jeff is shy, lives indoors, and is not currently accepting visitors, interviews, or requests for his autograph.
Is \"Jefferson\" his real name?: Yes, Jefferson Elmer is his real, government name. He arrived with the name "Jefferson", and when questioned about it, he just gives us a narrowed gaze and refuses to answer.
Why is his middle name Elmer?: I gave him that name because he looks like he was assembled with glue. Although I assure you, Jeff is (mostly) structurally sound.
How old is Jeff?: The shelter estimates Jeff to have been born around 2018. He has yet to provide us with a birth certificate.
Does Jeff know about this website?: Yes, he has been informed. When I told him, he stared at me for several seconds and then left the room, which his representatives describe as "neither approval nor disapproval".
Did Jeff approve these pictures?: Jeff was given several opportunities to comment. He responded by biting the corner of the release form.
Why does Jeff look different in every pi: Photots have been captured with variable lighting, cameras, settings, camera angles, and the possibility that he may be using other cats that are similar in appearance as stand-ins for his public appearances.
Why are there exactly 150 pictures?: Only 100 photos failed to capture the full range of Jeff's personality. However, 151 would have been excessive.
Will you add more pictures?: Probably not. The website has limited storage, and Jeff's complete photographic archive could threaten the structural integrity of Github.
Why did I see the same picture again?: The website avoids repeating pictures that have been recently displayed, but previously discovered ones can eventually return. Jeff believes that every photograph of him demands an encore.
Where is my progress saved?: Your discoveries and settings are stored locally in your browser. Clearing your brownser data or changing browsers gives Jeff the opportunity to pretend that you have never met.
Why are there \"Meet Jeff\" stickers?: Stickers were given to friends and family with instructions to place them alongside other stickers in designated public-art spaces. If you found a sticker and arrived here, then the Jeff experiment has succeeded.
This sticker shouldn't be here. How can: Whoops, sorry about that. I apologize. You can remove the sticker by catching the corner with a blade and peeling slowly. It's vinyl, so it should peel off in one piece. Any leftover residue can be cleaned with hydrogen peroxide.
